_readme: Every input to impact_model.py. kind: data = a number printed in the source; derived = arithmetic on data rows (formula given); assumption = our judgement, not data. verified: true = read in the primary source on the date given; false = taken from the repo's research notes or a secondary source and not re-read; null = assumption (nothing to verify).
_japan_role: Japan is used only because it publishes an end-of-life mass balance. Its numbers convert 'one attributable percentage point' into tonnes and CO2e for a market of that size. They are NOT an estimate of impact in Japan: there recovery is mandated and already tracked electronically (RaMS), so alpha is about 0, and Japanese recovery would likely fail a regulatory-surplus test for credits.

moej_2026.title: Ministry of the Environment, Japan: OEWG48 side-event presentation, 15 July 2026, slide 6 'Material Flow of HFCs Refrigerants in Japan (2024)' (marked 'based on current available data. It will be further examined')

jraia_2012.title: JRAIA (K. Sato): Actions to Control Emission of HFCs in Japan, regional symposium; recovery chart 2007-2012, 'recovery ratio is around 30%'

jraia_2017.title: JRAIA presentation 2017: FY2015 recovery at disposal approx. 3,499 t, 'approx. 38% of potential total disposing gases'

jraia_2019.title: JRAIA presentation 2019: recovery at disposal 'nearly 40% in 2017'; 2019 amendment (direct penalties, recovery certificates) aims at 'more than 70% in 2030'

jraia_2025.title: JRAIA (Ms. Yamanaka), OEWG47 side event, July 2025, slide 10: recovery rate 'Improved from 40% to 44%. This might be the effect of the revised Act' (years not stated)

eia_2026_banks.title: EIA (C. Mercado, D. Brack), Evaluating Options for Sustainably Financed Action on ODS and HFC Banks, May 2026. PDF p.24: TEAP MCTOC estimates 250,000-400,000 t of controlled ODS and HFCs decommissioned annually from the RACHP and foams sectors globally; mature programmes in Australia, Japan and the EU capture only 20-30% of end-of-life refrigerant. PDF p.21: New Zealand's ETS 'has helped increase refrigerant recovery rates from end-of-life equipment to 11 per cent'.

ccl_2024_reclamation.title: Carbon Containment Lab, Technical Note on HFC Reclamation, June 2024: when virgin suppliers expend all their quota, 'reclaimers do not displace any virgin refrigerant supply'; US 2022: 271.7 million of 273.5 million allowances expended (0.65% unused)

eu_fgas_2024_573.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/573 on fluorinated greenhouse gases, Annexes (GWP values from IPCC AR4)
eu_fgas_2024_573.checked: not re-read in this session; values as recorded in simulator/params.json (verified: true there)

eia_2026_via_refindustry.title: EIA report (Apr 2026) on illegal HFC trade into EU supply chains, as reported by refindustry: EU seizures about 250 t (2023) and about 670 t (2024)
eia_2026_via_refindustry.checked: not re-read in this session; from docs/research/02-validation-notes/verify_fgas_ledger.md

eu_price_monitoring_q4_2025.title: EU refrigerant price monitoring (Oeko-Recherche / CITEPA), Q4/2025 excerpt: reclaimed R-404A at about 140% of virgin price in Q1 2025
eu_price_monitoring_q4_2025.checked: not re-read in this session; from docs/proposal/03_第十輪反思_評審視角.md

skatteetaten_hfc.title: Norwegian Tax Administration: excise duty on HFC and PFC, with a refund per kg of gas delivered for destruction (administered by the Norwegian Environment Agency)
skatteetaten_hfc.checked: 2026-10-17, page read; it gives no evaluation of the refund's effect on recovery

japan_remaining_at_disposal_t.note: The slide's own total is 55 t less than recovered + emitted (12,066 t); the slide mixes fiscal-year reports and calendar-year inventory estimates.

japan_reclaimed_t.note: HFC reclaimed after recovery (6.85 MtCO2e on the slide); covers gas recovered at disposal and during maintenance (1,077 t).

japan_destroyed_t.note: HFC destroyed after recovery (5.38 MtCO2e on the slide). A further 65 t was 're-filled and recycled'.

points.rate: 40% -> 44%, 'might be the effect of the revised Act'

global_decommissioned_t_per_yr.note: TEAP MCTOC estimate quoted by EIA. Controlled ODS AND HFCs, refrigeration/AC/heat pumps AND foams, so it is a ceiling for HFC refrigerant. Used only as a tonnage scale reference; not converted to CO2e because the GWP mix is not given.

eu_seizures_t.kind: data (context only, not used in any calculation)

reclaimed_r404a_price_vs_virgin_q1_2025.kind: data (context only, not used in any calculation)

M_t.note: Refrigerant left in equipment scrapped in a Japan-sized market (Japan 2024). Tornado low case uses the slide's own total, 12,011 t.

gwp_emitted_mix.note: Average GWP of the gas that escaped at disposal. Tornado low case: the recovered gas mix, (21.85 - 12.62) Mt / 5,188 t.

permanence_destroyed_share.note: Headline (conservative) permanence: only the destroyed share of extra recovered gas counts. Under a binding quota, reclaimed gas adds to supply instead of displacing virgin gas (ccl_2024_reclamation), so its avoided emission is at most a delay.

permanence_full_displacement.note: Upper variant: every extra recovered tonne counts, as if reclaimed gas displaced virgin gas one for one (only possible where the quota does not bind).

beta_disposal_only.note: Share of gas reaching disposal that escapes; ignores leaks during use.

beta_flow.note: Share of the gas leaving Japan's 2024 equipment stock that was emitted rather than recovered at disposal.

delta_r_pp.unit: percentage points of the disposal recovery rate
delta_r_pp.why: Under penalty-backed law Japan's rate went from around 30% (2007-12) to 43% (2024), at most about 1 pp a year, with no reform's effect cleanly identified (no 2013-14 data; JRAIA only says the 40% to 44% rise 'might be' the 2019 revision), and New Zealand's carbon-priced scheme reached 11% recovery; a voluntary data layer is weaker than a law, so the mode is 1 pp, the maximum 5 pp is just above the largest hedged single-reform change (4 pp), and 0 is a real possibility.

alpha.applies_to: a market where paid-for recovery is held back by unverifiable claims (e.g. credits or reclaimed premiums where fraud is a concern). In Japan itself alpha is about 0.
alpha.why: No study separates the effect of verifiability from the effect of the payment itself: alpha can be 0 (refund schemes such as Norway's pay on delivered gas without a shared ledger) and stays below 1 because the payment, not the ledger, is the direct cause; the mode of 0.3 is below the 0.5-0.7 used in the proposal.

beta.unit: share of a blocked tonne that would eventually have been emitted
beta.why: Anchored to Japan's 2024 flows: 0.57 is the disposal-only escape share (it ignores leaks during use, so it is a floor for a Japan-like recovery regime), 0.72 is the share of all gas leaving the stock that was emitted, and 0.95 stands for markets with little end-of-life recovery; no EU equivalent of Japan's flow table was verified, so Japan is used as a proxy.

pilot._note: Inputs to the rough pilot-size calculation. All are conventions or assumptions, not data.

baseline_unit_recovery_share.note: Uses Japan's mass recovery rate as a stand-in for the share of scrapped units with a recovery; per-unit data were not found.

cluster_example.note: Design effect = 1 + (m - 1) x ICC for clustering by technician or site; no measured ICC was found.
